requirements.requirement: Forward inventory-tagged log messages from node2 to the centralized collector on node1.
requirements.summary: A baseline inventory-tagged message from node2 established a TCP connection to node1 and was observed at the collector. The collector remained active and listening on its managed address.

requirements.requirement: Persist received node2 inventory messages on node1 at /var/log/inventory/node2.log.
requirements.summary: The required file existed with restrictive permissions and contained the baseline message plus messages generated after both restart tests.

requirements.requirement: Keep the logging flow working after either node1 or node2 restarts.
requirements.summary: Both nodes had healthy pre-restart states, acknowledged restart scheduling, became temporarily unavailable, returned with different boot IDs, and recovered rsyslog operation. A new inventory message reached the persistent file after each restart, while earlier data remained present. Fixed lifecycle boot observations independently confirm both boot-ID changes.

overall_summary: All material outcomes are satisfied. Inventory-tagged messages were forwarded from node2, persisted at the required node1 path, and successfully delivered after independent restarts of both managed nodes. The provider-wide restart protocol is complete and corroborated by lifecycle boot identities.
limitations: End-to-end tests used synthetic messages emitted with logger under the inventory tag rather than evidence of a real inventory application process. This directly exercises the configured routing path but does not independently establish the application's own logging behavior.
Pre-executor package-health checks timed out, so package consistency cannot be compared directly across lifecycle phases; post-executor checks were healthy on both nodes.

operational_hygiene.summary: No unnecessary mutations were identified. Configuration-file creation, directory creation, firewall changes, rsyslog restarts, synthetic test messages, and both system restarts were causally connected to implementing or directly verifying the required forwarding and restart persistence. No failed services, abandoned temporary artifacts, package damage, or unrelated exposure was observed; TCP/514 was bound only to node1's managed address and firewalled to node2.
